short: Host existence on windows from a cohomology bound

statements.markdown: Statement 9.1 (supplyChi). For every primitive ψ, if the cohomological bound holds for ψ with exponent 401, then hosts with the required properties exist at every scale in a set containing windows of exponent 32 .

lean.name: UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi
lean.plain: Host existence on windows from a cohomology bound
lean.fidelity_note: The premise is $VWinAt(\psi,401)$. Lean fixes the constants and threshold for each $0<\varepsilon<1/52$, then gives hosts at every scale above the threshold in a set containing arbitrarily late windows $[Y,Y^{3/2}]$. Each host carries both the explicit-formula input and the square-root cohomology bound at its actual block width.

statements.markdown: The only assumption about ψ is its cohomological bound. The windows come from Statement 8.1, which holds on windows [Y 1 , Y 1 2 ]; this is why Statement 4.1 is needed in its windowed form.

lean.name: UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi
lean.plain: Host existence on windows from a cohomology bound
lean.note: `supplyChi` takes only $VWinAt(\psi,401)$. Its helper calls `winPairs` with the proved `QH.pairEx`, and the resulting windows enter the scale set in `HostExW`.

lean.name: UpperTheory.Top.VWin
lean.plain: Windowed cohomology bounds for every primitive character
lean.note: `VWin` is $VWinAt(\psi,401)$ for every primitive $\psi$. For each $\varepsilon$ and eligible schedule of cyclotomic layers, `VWinAt` chooses $J$, then gives a square window inside $[X^{1/J},X]$ for every sufficiently large $X$ and every prime pair eligible at $X^{1/J}$.
